city.Washington DC.description: The capital of the United States sits on the Potomac River and is known for the White House, the domed Capitol, and monuments along the National Mall.
city.Washington DC.greeting: English is spoken here — a polite hello is “Hi there” (hy thair).
city.Washington DC.flag: fifty white stars on blue with thirteen red-and-white stripes
city.Washington DC.clue.0: studied a map of an American capital lined with gleaming marble monuments
city.Washington DC.clue.1: planned to stroll a grassy mall between a domed capitol and a white house
city.Washington DC.clue.2: boasted of climbing to the top of a tall, pointed riverside obelisk
city.Algeria.description: Algeria is the biggest country in all of Africa, and the vast Sahara Desert covers most of it. In the deep south live the Tuareg, desert nomads known for the bright indigo-blue veils that earn them the nickname the “blue people.” Couscous is the star of its kitchens.
city.Algeria.landmark: vast golden Sahara sand dunes with the jagged volcanic Hoggar Mountains rising in the distance
city.Algeria.flag: green and white with a red crescent moon and a red star
city.Algeria.clue.0: booked a ticket toward the biggest country in all of Africa
city.Algeria.clue.1: dreamed of riding a camel across endless golden dunes in the Sahara Desert
city.Angola.description: Angola sits on the southwest coast of Africa, where the cool Atlantic Ocean meets the dunes of the Namib Desert. It is rich in oil and sparkling diamonds, and most people here speak Portuguese.
city.Angola.flag: red and black with a golden star, a machete, and half of a gear wheel
city.Angola.clue.0: kept practicing Portuguese words, excited for a big country on Africa's southwest coast
city.Benin.description: Benin is a slim country in West Africa and the birthplace of Vodun, which you may know as Voodoo. Long ago the Kingdom of Dahomey was guarded by the Agojie, a famous army of women warriors.
city.Benin.landmark: stilt-house village of Ganvié standing over the calm waters of Lake Nokoué
city.Benin.flag: a green stripe down the side, with yellow and red bands beside it
city.Benin.clue.0: circled a narrow sliver of West Africa on a map
city.Benin.clue.1: read about colorful festivals full of drums, masks and dancing, in the land where Voodoo began
city.Benin.clue.2: read all about fierce women warriors who once guarded an ancient kingdom
city.Botswana.description: This dry, landlocked country in Southern Africa is famous for the watery maze of the Okavango Delta, huge herds of elephants, and diamonds mined from beneath its sands.
city.Botswana.landmark: elephants wading among the reed islands and water channels of the Okavango Delta
city.Botswana.greeting: In Setswana you greet someone with “Dumela” (doo-MEH-lah).
